chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: The Bandbox and the Rhythm Club as musicians' hangouts
summary: The Rhythm Club, newer and with a pool table, drew musicians away from the Bandbox one corner over on Seventh Avenue.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Now, in these early days, was there a Rhythm Club then where everybody collected? Or was it the Bandbox?

Well, they used to collect around the Bandbox, and then the Bandbox was... The Rhythm Club was opened by a fellow who come from Chicago. He opened up the Rhythm Club right around the corner from the Bandbox, the next corner. And it was a better-looking place, it was a larger place -- it had a pool table there. So naturally,
the fellas went around the corner. And that kind of taken all the crowd away from the Bandbox.
Where was it? Do you remember the street?

Yeah. That was One Hundred Thirty-Second Street and Seventh Avenue. The Bandbox was One Hundred Thirty-First Street and Seventh Avenue. So it was right around the corner. But it was a better place, it was a newer place, and it was a lively place. All the musicians talkin' and hangin' in there. The Bandbox finally faded out.
